avatars.pose: Cheeky grin with sword resting across his shoulders
avatars.prompt:
ONE ORIGINAL FAN ART PROFILE PORTRAIT of the male IOP / YOPUKA from DOFUS. The attached references are three views of his actual game model. Keep him immediately recognizable as THIS Dofus class: tall flame-shaped tangerine-orange hair, the characteristic long cheek-framing orange side locks, long pointed ears, tan slim angular face, expressive solid-white pupil-less eyes, bone-white sleeveless tunic with teal-blue neck/armhole edging and large dark red stylized sword/cross on chest, single rounded crimson pauldron. Keep these design features and exact local clothing colors. Do not redesign as generic fantasy, do not add a cape or scarf, do not borrow characters from other games.
The creative brief is a PERSONALITY-FILLED FAN DRAWING, combining an inventive expressive pose with an unmistakably crafted INK AND WATERCOLOR finish. Like a beautiful original drawing from a character illustrator's sketchbook, digitally finished but retaining its drawing decisions.
NEW POSE AND EXPRESSION: the Iop leans a little toward the viewer, shoulders turned one way and head turned back toward us, with a bold lopsided cheeky grin showing just his upper teeth, one eye squinted slightly more than the other, exuberant slightly foolish bravery. He is casually resting his oversized sword across the BACK of his shoulders; only a simple section of blade and guard behind him should be visible. The sword must not cross or hide his face. Convey a lively affectionate understanding of Iop personality. Three-quarter eye-level portrait, not the game's top-down camera or idle stance. Slightly exaggerated lively original Dofus comic anatomy, prominent expressive ears, face drawn with charm and asymmetry. Composition for a profile photo: ONE head-and-shoulders character, face near center, tall hair fully contained with empty space above, face and hair read inside central circular crop. Shoulders can run out at bottom.
DRAWING LANGUAGE: visible lively dark graphite preliminary strokes in a few places, confident tapered black brush-pen ink with a mix of hairline marks and heavier expressive contour, a few selective hatch marks. Actual linework should be the beauty of the picture. Hand-placed loose watercolor fills with occasional small unfilled paper gaps near ink edges, beautiful limited colors, natural varied watercolor edges; quiet matte finish. Keep the planes SIMPLE, crisp shapes on the main silhouette and loose little drawn decisions inside. Color slightly understated, not fluorescent. Background is clean warm off-white with one restrained loose desaturated teal watercolor wash behind the character, irregular and unobtrusive. No artificial all-over grain filter, no grunge overlay, no brown paper, no perfect vector lines or mechanically uniform edge, no over-rendered digital painting, no plastic or 3D, no gloss, no cinematic glow, no rim lighting, no airbrushed gradients, no sparks, no over-detailed hair strands, no decoration or fake handwritten notes. The drawing should feel FUN, OBSERVED, CHARACTERFUL, PERSONAL, not a polished generic AI avatar or tracing of the reference.
Square opaque image. Single character only, not a sheet, no collage, no frame, no text, no signature, no watermark, no lettering.

This is the SIXTH selectable FACE/HAIRSTYLE, not an alternate outfit; keep the DEFAULT original costume. Installed client: DOFUS 3.7.14.18. IMAGE 1 is the APPROVED INK-AND-WATERCOLOR TECHNIQUE ONLY. IMAGES 2 and 3 show the exact SIXTH target game face from two angles, head skin 2033, body skin 20; IMAGE 4 shows the same complete game model for species, arm, hand and outfit continuity. Preserve the precise selected head silhouette, mask/eyepatch/headwear, eye type, species, original colors and usual outfit. Never import Iop hair, sword, eyes, anatomy or pose from image 1 into another class.
Sixth male head: pale ivory-blond high swept crest with BIG asymmetric heavy fringe sweeping across OWN LEFT forehead near eye, long thin temple locks to jaw, two small ivory horns with black bases emerging from sides of hair, large pointed ears, vivid RED irises. Usual teal sleeveless close-fit tunic with golden shoulder rims and collar, narrow ivory central stripe, black bracers and bare hands. Preserve exact sixth broad swept fringe, not fifth smaller separated center fringe.
NEW INDIVIDUAL POSE AND EXPRESSION: A playful summoner calling a distant companion with a soft whistle: lips gently rounded, one eyebrow raised, chin lifted toward own RIGHT and chest turned the opposite way. Both shoulders relaxed, arms angle DOWN and hands are entirely below chest-up crop. A lively slight backward head tilt conveys the call, no creature visible. No bird, treat, whip handle, coil or stroking pose. Horns and full hair silhouette contained. Make a distinctive living fan-art drawing, not a copy or recolor of an earlier pose. Identity and unobscured defining head features take priority over gesture.
STYLE: match image 1 confident varied-weight tapered black ink, selective graphite construction strokes and hatching, expressive French fantasy comic drawing, economical readable forms, matte loose watercolor with hand-placed pigment edges and small paper gaps. Rich slightly understated actual game colors, warm off-white paper and a restrained irregular muted sunflower yellow and dusty turquoise wash. No artificial grunge, glossy digital fantasy painting, plastic/3D, photorealism, airbrushed gradients, cinematic bloom or vector-perfect shapes.
Square opaque background included. One HEAD AND UPPER TORSO, face large near the center, complete defining hairstyle/headwear with top breathing room, readable inside centered circular avatars at 150 and 48 pixels. Shoulders may crop at the bottom. Only the specified small relevant prop. Do not introduce text, lettering, signatures, labels, logos, watermarks, borders, collage or multiple views.
ANATOMY REVIEW BEFORE DELIVERY: Trace exactly two continuous arms from one pair of shoulders to two wrists and hands; overlapping forearms must not imply extra limbs. Inspect shoulder/back skin strips and every sleeve cuff: a narrow extra limb behind a shoulder or a second cuff can suggest a third arm even when the hands are correct. For a user-marked defect, inspect and correct that exact region while retaining their selected reference and gesture. Check handedness and thumb position. Human hands have four fingers plus one thumb; make all five digits readable when the pose exposes the whole hand. Inspect each finger root and natural gripping contact, especially behind props: never add a detached, superimposed or excessively hooked thumb to force a five-digit count. Keep animal hands furry with their real claws and game species. Respect naturally occluded digits. Check one coherent clothed ribcage and torso, with no duplicate shoulder, torso or chest-shaped folds. Inspect the large artwork and the small circular crop separately. Preserve the real selected game head and usual outfit while correcting anatomy. For edits, keep the original generation prompt and immutable source PNG, save the exact edit prompt and reference roles/hashes, then update both native PNG and WebP. In particular, exactly two continuous arms from a single pair of shoulders, only one sleeve/cuff per arm, one coherent torso and chest. Correct right/left hands and thumb roots; four fingers plus one thumb for fully exposed humanlike hands, clearly readable separate tips. Natural occlusion for curled fingers. Respect feline/canine/panda fur and the actual skeletal or wrapped game anatomy. Inspect the entire portrait, not only its hands.
CRITICAL AVATAR FRAMING: leave at least 8 percent warm paper breathing room ABOVE the highest hair/hat tip. Keep the complete defining hairstyle and ears within the middle 80 percent width; do not let a ponytail or hat touch an image edge. Use a comfortably pulled-back bust framing. No hand may be accidentally revealed as a partial extra limb at the lower edge.
